observations.why: The directive frames successful pipeline output as a capability requirement — the system must be able to produce a slug and commit — appealing to competence as the good.
The modal 'must' enacts a directive imposing an obligation on the pipeline — a hierarchical command structure where the speaker mandates behavior.
Deontic 'must' with a process-failure scenario carries urgency-as-pressure, placing the speaker in high-arousal negative territory.
Deontic 'must' asserts a process obligation grounded in agreed-upon pipeline requirements, with a success criterion that functions as insistence on compliance.

positions.name: MissingIdPipelineObligation
positions.frame: What must the pipeline do when a memory is submitted without an explicit id field?
positions.why: src-1 states the triggering condition — a memory submitted without an explicit id — as a settled, unhedged fact (claim-grade, present-realis). src-2 states the operational mandate that answers that condition — the pipeline must produce a slug via LLM id-gen or deterministic fallback and commit successfully (decision-grade, future-irrealis, technical register with deontic 'must'). The two cohere as condition-and-mandate under one read: the pipeline's obligation when identity is absent. The conviction gradient (claim vs decision) is the natural arc from problem-statement to required-behavior, not a disqualifying split.

placements.why: The content specifies pipeline behavior as a deontic mandate — what the system must do (produce a slug, commit the file) and through which mechanisms (LLM id-gen call, deterministic slugify fallback). This names an organizational category for system design and behavior that nothing in the existing strata or structure covers.

Together they name a subject future envelopes will keep feeding — the pipeline's identity-generation behavior when identity is absent — which passes the grain test: it is true beyond the words it describes, not a one-time measurement or event.
